speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) what specific factors have contributed to the lower hiring rate of Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) in the public sector compared to the private sector; (b) how the hiring rate of PwDs in Singapore’s Public Service quantitatively compares with that in other developed countries; (c) what structural or policy-related constraints prevent Singapore Government agencies from increasing PwD hires; and (d) what steps are being taken to address these constraints directly.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The hon Member also asked about the constraints of hiring PwDs and steps taken to address these constraints.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Member may refer to the responses to the Parliamentary Question (PQ) that he raised on 15 October, and the PQ raised by the Member, Mr Don Wee, on 9 September, where we shared the public sector's approach to the issue.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The public sector has been and will continue to support the employment of PwDs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I understand that the Minister said that is not meaningful to compare.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I would just like more clarification on why he thinks that is not meaningful, apart from the fact that the Singapore Armed Forces and the Home Team may not be able to hire as many PwDs in combat positions.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: As the largest employer in Singapore, does the Minister agree that the Government bears a greater responsibility to set a positive hiring example in inclusive hiring?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Ideally, the public sector should lead the hiring of PwDs, rather than lagging behind.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are not here just to meet the numbers.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Speaker, I want to declare, first, that I am a volunteer actively helping job centres in inclusive employment.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am quite excited about the work that is going on in inclusive employment in the public sector.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Actually, I think that they have done quite a bit in inclusive hiring, sometimes not allowing us in the charity sector to give up even.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The average rate does not reflect some of the very good work that is done.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are also critical success factors that I hope the Minister will agree with me that we can learn from.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The first is top leadership engagement and support, middle management focus, job design, equipping the colleagues and encouraging those on the ground.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, quite a bit of critical success factors.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And, in fact, position the public sector strongly as a leader in inclusive employment.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There is a lot of room there and I am very encouraged by the hiring so far.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, we have groups of civil servants who are passionate about this and they go about doing their work quietly to make sure that jobs that can be converted, or even modified, to take in PwDs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have done so and will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We want to make sure that every job counts, rather than count every job.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is important for us that we employ PwDs to give them meaningful work, rather than just to meet any numerical targets.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And as what Ms Denise Phua has mentioned, it is important that we continue this journey, not only with top-level management attention on this, but it also requires every one of us who is working in the sector to make accommodations and adjustments, so that we can bring out the best in everyone, including PwDs.
